from.place: the proof's opening comparison principle: precomposition by a quasi-isomorphism induces a bijection on morphisms into a K-injective complex

title: Comparison principle for a K-injective target
statement:
Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian] for which the derived category exists. If $s:A\to B$ is a quasi-isomorphism of cochain complexes and $I$ is K-injective [def-sp-kinjective-bridge], then precomposition induces a bijection

$$
 s^*:\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal A)}(B,I)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal A)}(A,I).
$$

proof.text: Let Q:K(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal A) be the localization. For each complex N, the map Q on morphisms Hom_{K(\mathcal A)}(N,I)\to Hom_{D(\mathcal A)}(QN,QI) is bijective because I is K-injective, by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]. Apply this for N=A and N=B.

Since s is a quasi-isomorphism, the localization Q(s):Q(A)\to Q(B) is an isomorphism in D(\mathcal A), by the definition of the derived category as the localization at quasi-isomorphisms. Therefore precomposition by Q(s) is a bijection Hom_D(QB,QI)\to Hom_D(QA,QI), with inverse given by precomposition by Q(s)^{-1}.

The localization functor is functorial, so Q(g\circ s)=Q(g)\circ Q(s). The two bijections from step 1 conjugate precomposition by s with precomposition by Q(s); hence precomposition by s is bijective. This is exactly the asserted map s^*:Hom_{K(\mathcal A)}(B,I)\to Hom_{K(\mathcal A)}(A,I).
